summary: Backend regression + logic verification of the refactored recipe pricing engine. 19/19 tests PASSED. Core bug fix verified: suggested_sell_price now correctly equals $237.97 (was $273.66 pre-fix) for food=71.39, overhead=15%, target_food=30%, portions=1. New pricing_methods object (food_cost_method / prime_cost_method / gross_margin_markup) present with correct math. Per-portion catering math verified (10 portions -> cost/portion=7.14, suggested=~23.80). Company settings persist new target_prime_cost_percent (55) and target_gross_margin_percent (65). Proposals-recipe link intact. No regressions found.

minor.issue: dry_run is declared as a query param (bool = True), so sending {"dry_run": false} in JSON body is silently ignored. Only ?dry_run=false query string works. Consider accepting body too, or documenting explicitly.
Not a route - menus live under /api/settings/menus. Just a documentation note (original review_request referenced /api/menus which returns 404).

action_items: OPTIONAL: consider allowing recalculate-all to accept dry_run in JSON body (client convenience).
critical_code_review_comments: compute_full_recipe_costing (server.py 2930-3049): clean implementation, well-commented, correctly uses food_cost only for Method A (bug is truly fixed).
server.py is 24,271 lines — should be split into modular routers.
target_food_pct=0 edge case falls back to suggested_sell_price=0; acceptable but no explicit warning surfaced to the client.
seed_data_creation: Test creates ephemeral TEST_ prefixed ingredients + recipes with UUID suffixes; each fixture cleans up in teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression test file at /app/backend/tests/test_recipe_pricing_methods.py covers pricing engine end-to-end (settings CRUD, single-portion math $237.97, catering per-portion math, recalculate-all, pricing_methods panel structure & math, proposals-recipe link, menu-engineering, cost-preview fallback). Run with: pytest backend/tests/test_recipe_pricing_methods.py -v
rca of the issue: Original bug: prior formula was suggested_sell_price = total_cost / target_food% which included overhead in the numerator AND applied a food-cost target percentage denominator, so overhead was effectively counted twice. Fixed formula (line 2992) uses cost_per_portion_food (food only) as numerator, restoring standard restaurant-industry Method A: sell = food / target_food%. Verified: 71.39/0.30 = 237.97.
